uiLanguage.name: Module language
uiLanguage.hint: The language of the Performance Doctor on this computer.

theme.name: Look
theme.hint: Warm paper colors or the dark colors of Foundry, for you.

autoPrompt.name: Offer help when the game is slow
autoPrompt.hint: When your frame rate stays very low for about a minute, a small window offers help. Once per session at most.

shareWithGM.name: Share my numbers with the GM
shareWithGM.hint: Sends your frame rate, delay, download speed, graphics chip and scene load times to the GMs, so they can help. Nothing goes to other players.

attribution.name: Note which module registers what
attribution.hint: Needed for the module measurement: the doctor notes which package registers each hook and ticker callback. Costs no noticeable time. Needs a reload.

gmAlerts.name: Alerts for the GM
gmAlerts.hint: Notifications when a player waits long for a scene, cannot load images or has a serious problem.

slowLoadSeconds.name: Slow scene load after
slowLoadSeconds.hint: Seconds after which a player's scene load counts as slow.

sceneWarnings.name: Warn about heavy scenes
sceneWarnings.hint: When you activate a scene or add a very large image, the doctor checks the size and warns you.

open.name: Performance Doctor
open.label: Open the Performance Doctor
open.hint: Find out why the game is slow and fix it.

Keybinding.openHint: Opens the window with the status of your game.

Banner.gmAsked: {name} asked you to check your game. The hints below show what helps.

noAcceleration.title: Your browser draws without the graphics card
noAcceleration.text: That is the most common reason for very low frame rates. The first hint below shows how to switch it on.

noCanvas.title: No game board
noCanvas.text: The canvas is off or no scene is open, so there are no frames to measure.

waiting.title: Measuring…
waiting.text: The doctor needs a few seconds with a map on screen.

hidden.title: Foundry is in the background
hidden.text: Bring the Foundry tab to the front to measure.

smooth.title: Your game runs smoothly
smooth.text: {fps} frames per second, the goal is {target}.

fair.title: Your game runs a bit slow
fair.text: {fps} frames per second, the goal is {target}.

slow.title: Your game is slow
slow.text: {fps} frames per second, the goal is {target}.

Live.fpsHint: Frames per second of the map over the last seconds. 60 is smooth, below 20 it stutters.
Live.latencyHint: How long a message needs to the server and back.
Live.speedHint: Download speed from the server, from the files your browser loaded or from the connection test.
Live.sparkHint: Frames per second of the last minute

Overview.playersTrouble: Players with a problem or loading: {count} of {total}.
Overview.allGood: Nothing to fix. Have a good game!

Wizard.title: Make my game faster
Wizard.intro: Measures your game for ten seconds, suggests the settings that help most and checks the result. Everything can be undone.
Wizard.measuringHint: Keep the map open and move it around a little.
Wizard.measured: Your game ran at {fps} frames per second.
Wizard.nothing: No Foundry setting is left that would help much. The hints below explain the other causes.
Wizard.reloadText: One change needs a reload. After the reload the doctor measures again and shows the result.
Wizard.still: Still slow? The graphics test and the module measurement look deeper.
Wizard.noCanvas: The assistant needs a scene on the canvas.

Reload.title: Reload needed
Reload.text: This change takes effect after a reload of Foundry. Reload now?

Fix.applied: Setting changed. "Undo my changes" in the tab This computer puts it back.

softwareRenderer.title: Your browser draws without the graphics card
softwareRenderer.text: Foundry runs on "{gpu}", a software stand-in: the processor has to draw every frame itself. That alone brings the game down to a few frames per second, even on a strong computer. Switch on hardware acceleration in your browser and restart it.

noWebGL2.title: Your browser offers only old graphics features
noWebGL2.text: Foundry needs WebGL 2. Update your browser and your graphics driver.

oldBrowser.title: Your browser is too old for this Foundry version
oldBrowser.text: {browser} is older than Foundry needs. Older versions are slower and may show errors.

noCanvas.title: The game board is switched off
noCanvas.text: "Disable Game Canvas" is on in Foundry's settings. That is very light, but you see no map.

hiddenTab.title: Measuring needs the Foundry tab in front
hiddenTab.text: Browsers slow down tabs in the background. Bring Foundry to the front for a few seconds.

fpsCapped.title: Your frame rate is limited to {max} frames per second
fpsCapped.text: Your computer could draw more. For smoother movement allow 60 frames per second.

slowCpu.title: Your game is slow: {fps} frames per second
slowCpu.text: The processor is busy with scripts for {cpu} % of every frame. Often a module or a busy scene causes it. The module measurement shows who uses the time.

slowGpu.title: Your game is slow: {fps} frames per second
slowGpu.text: The scripts are quick, so the drawing itself is too much for your graphics chip. Lower quality settings help most. The graphics test shows which effect costs the most.

hidpi.title: Foundry draws at {dpr} times the screen resolution
hidpi.text: Your screen is scaled, so Foundry draws {factor} times as many pixels as the window shows. Turning off resolution scaling makes the picture a little softer and often helps a lot.

modeHigh.title: The graphics quality is set high
modeHigh.text: High and maximum quality add soft light edges and finer detail. Medium looks almost the same and costs less.

modeMedium.title: Even medium quality is too much for this computer
modeMedium.text: Low quality switches off soft edges and some animations.

lightAnimation.title: Animated lights are on
lightAnimation.text: Flickering torches and pulsing lights are redrawn in every frame. Without animation the light stays, it only stops moving.

visionAnimation.title: Animated vision is on
visionAnimation.text: Vision modes with movement are redrawn in every frame.

integratedGpu.title: Foundry runs on the built-in graphics ({gpu})
integratedGpu.text: Many laptops have a second, stronger graphics card. Windows decides which one the browser uses, and you can choose.

battery.title: Your laptop runs on battery ({level} %)
battery.text: On battery many laptops slow down the graphics and the browser saves energy. Plug in the charger or set the power mode to best performance.

fps30.title: Your game is stuck at about 30 frames per second
fps30.text: That is often the energy saver of the browser or of Windows. It halves the frame rate to save power.

largeCanvas.title: Your window is very large ({mp} megapixels)
largeCanvas.text: A 4K screen has four times the pixels of Full HD. A smaller browser window or resolution scaling off helps the graphics chip.

tryChromium.title: Try Chrome or Edge for comparison
tryChromium.text: On the same computer Foundry often runs faster in Chrome or Edge than in Firefox.

blocked.title: Scripts block your browser ({share} % of the time)
blocked.text: Now and then the browser freezes for a moment because a script runs too long. The module measurement shows which one.

memoryFull.title: The browser memory is almost full
memoryFull.text: Foundry uses {used} of {limit}. A reload frees it. If it fills up again soon, a module or a very large world may be the cause.

textureMemory.title: Images take {bytes} of graphics memory
textureMemory.text: That is a lot for many graphics cards. Smaller maps and token images help.

latencyHigh.title: The connection to the server is slow ({ms})
latencyHigh.text: Every move and every roll needs a trip to the server and back. Above 300 ms it feels sluggish.

connectionDrops.title: Requests the server did not answer: {count}
connectionDrops.text: Your connection drops now and then. Wi-Fi, a VPN or a busy line are common causes.

slowLine.title: Your download speed is low ({speed})
slowLine.text: A map of {map} takes about {ms} to load at this speed.

saveData.title: Data saver is on
saveData.text: Your browser saves data and may load images more slowly.

sceneHeavy.title: This scene is large: {bytes} to download
sceneHeavy.text: Every player downloads it when the scene opens, at your speed in about {ms}. The GM can make the images smaller with this module.

sceneTooLargeForGpu.title: An image of this scene is too large for your graphics chip
sceneTooLargeForGpu.text: It is {side} pixels on its longest side, your graphics chip shows at most {max}. It may stay black. A smaller copy fixes it: tell the GM.

sceneDownload.title: Players download {bytes} for this scene
sceneDownload.text: On an average line (16 Mbit/s) that takes about {typical}. Smaller copies of the largest images help the most.

sceneDownloadPlayer.title: Players download {bytes} for this scene
sceneDownloadPlayer.text: Your slowest player ({slowest}) needs about {ms}, an average line (16 Mbit/s) about {typical}. Smaller copies of the largest images help the most.

imageTooLargeForPlayers.title: {file} is too large for some graphics chips
imageTooLargeForPlayers.text: The image is {side} pixels on its longest side. For {players} it may stay black. A copy at 8192 pixels fixes it.

imageHeavy.title: {file} is {bytes}
imageHeavy.text: Large files make everyone wait when the scene opens. A WebP copy is usually several times smaller and looks the same.

videoHeavy.title: The video {file} is {bytes}
videoHeavy.text: Everyone downloads videos and decodes them all the time. A shorter or smaller WebM video (up to 1920 pixels) helps. The module cannot convert videos.

imageLarge.title: {file} is very large: {width} × {height} pixels
imageLarge.text: Above 8192 pixels many graphics chips struggle, above 16384 most cannot show it. Foundry stretches the image over the scene, so a smaller copy keeps walls and tokens in place.

imagePng.title: {file} is a PNG of {bytes}
imagePng.text: PNG keeps every pixel and is large for maps. WebP looks the same at a fraction of the size.

sceneGpuMemory.title: The images of this scene need {bytes} of graphics memory
sceneGpuMemory.text: Graphics chips with little memory slow down or drop images. Smaller images help.

sceneEmbedded.title: Images stored inside the scene data: {count}
sceneEmbedded.text: Images saved as text make the world data larger for everyone. Save them as files and use the paths.

walls.title: Many walls: {count}
walls.text: Every light and every token with vision checks the walls. Thousands of walls slow down movement and lighting.

lights.title: Many lights: {count}
lights.text: Each light is drawn and checked against the walls. Merge lights that sit close together.

animatedLights.title: Many animated lights: {count}
animatedLights.text: Animated lights are redrawn in every frame on every computer.

tokens.title: Many tokens: {count}
tokens.text: Hundreds of tokens cost every computer time. Move tokens nobody needs into another scene.

visionTokens.title: Many tokens with vision: {count}
visionTokens.text: Each vision source is computed against the walls. Most monster tokens do not need vision.

tiles.title: Many tiles: {count}
tiles.text: Each tile is an image the canvas has to draw.

videos.title: Several videos play: {count}
videos.text: Video tiles and backgrounds are decoded all the time on every computer.

drawings.title: Many drawings: {count}
drawings.text: Drawings, especially with text, cost time when drawing the canvas.

sounds.title: Many ambient sounds: {count}
sounds.text: Each sound checks its distance to tokens and walls.

moduleHeavy.title: {owner} uses {share} % of your computer's time
moduleHeavy.text: That is {ms} ms every second. Look at its settings for effects or animations, update it, or ask the GM whether the table needs it.

moduleSpike.title: {owner} blocks the game for up to {ms}
moduleSpike.text: One call ({label}) took that long, and the picture freezes meanwhile.

worldLarge.title: Every player downloads {bytes} when joining
worldLarge.text: Foundry sends the whole world (actors, items, journals, chat) to everyone who joins. Large worlds load slowly, especially on slow lines.

chatLarge.title: The chat log is large: {count} messages ({bytes})
chatLarge.text: Every player loads the whole chat when joining. Export the log and clear it now and then.

documentLarge.title: {name} is {bytes}
documentLarge.text: One of the largest documents of the world ({collection}). Embedded images or very long texts are typical causes.

documentImages.title: {name} carries embedded images ({count})
documentImages.text: Images pasted into texts are stored inside the document ({bytes}). Save them as files and link them instead.

packIndexes.title: Compendium indexes take {bytes}
packIndexes.text: Every active compendium sends its index on joining. Switch off modules whose compendiums you do not use.

scenesLarge.title: The scenes take {bytes} of world data
scenesLarge.text: Walls, lights and tokens of every scene are part of the world data. Delete or export scenes you no longer need.

fogLarge.title: Fog of war data takes {bytes} on the server
fogLarge.text: Explored areas are kept per scene and user. Reset the fog of old scenes.

manyModules.title: {count} modules are active
manyModules.text: Each module loads scripts and can take time. Switch off what this world does not use.

allSlowDownloads.title: All {count} players download slowly
allSlowDownloads.text: When everyone is slow, the bottleneck is often the server's upload, for example when Foundry runs at home. Smaller images help, or hosting with a fast line.

allHighLatency.title: All {count} players have a slow connection to the server
allHighLatency.text: When everyone is delayed, the server or its line is likely busy or far away.

playerProblem.title: {name}: {issue}
playerProblem.text: Ask the player to open the Performance Doctor (button next to the name). It explains the fix step by step.

Short.sceneTooLargeForGpu: Image too large for the graphics chip

accelChrome.title: Hardware acceleration in Chrome
accelChrome.steps:
Copy `chrome://settings/system` and paste it into the address bar of a new tab.
Switch on "Use graphics acceleration when available".
Click "Relaunch". Chrome opens your tabs again.
Open the Performance Doctor again: the warning should be gone.
accelChrome.outro: Was it on already? Then the browser lost the graphics card, often after a driver update. Restart the computer. If that does not help, update the graphics driver.

accelEdge.title: Hardware acceleration in Edge
accelEdge.steps:
Copy `edge://settings/system` and paste it into the address bar of a new tab.
Switch on "Use graphics acceleration when available".
Click "Restart". Edge opens your tabs again.
Open the Performance Doctor again: the warning should be gone.
accelEdge.outro: Was it on already? Then the browser lost the graphics card, often after a driver update. Restart the computer. If that does not help, update the graphics driver.

accelOpera.title: Hardware acceleration in Opera
accelOpera.steps:
Copy `opera://settings/system` and paste it into the address bar of a new tab.
Switch on "Use graphics acceleration when available".
Restart Opera.
accelOpera.outro: Was it on already? Restart the computer and update the graphics driver.

accelBrave.title: Hardware acceleration in Brave
accelBrave.steps:
Copy `brave://settings/system` and paste it into the address bar of a new tab.
Switch on "Use graphics acceleration when available".
Click "Relaunch".
accelBrave.outro: Was it on already? Restart the computer and update the graphics driver.

accelFirefox.title: Hardware acceleration in Firefox
accelFirefox.steps:
Open the menu ☰ → Settings → General and scroll down to Performance.
Untick "Use recommended performance settings".
Tick "Use hardware acceleration when available".
Restart Firefox.
accelFirefox.outro: To check: open `about:support`. Under Graphics, Compositing should say WebRender, not WebRender (Software).

accelSafari.title: Graphics in Safari
accelSafari.steps:
Safari always uses the graphics chip, there is no switch.
Update macOS: System Settings → General → Software Update.
Restart the Mac.
accelSafari.outro: If it stays slow, try the game in Chrome or Edge.

accelApp.title: The Foundry app runs without the graphics card
accelApp.steps:
Update your graphics driver (website of NVIDIA, AMD or Intel).
Restart the computer.
Windows: Settings → System → Display → Graphics, add the Foundry app and choose "High performance".
If it stays slow, open the game in Chrome or Edge: it runs the same in the browser.

drivers.title: Update the graphics driver
drivers.steps:
Look up the maker of your graphics chip in the tab This computer.
NVIDIA: `nvidia.com/drivers` · AMD: `amd.com/support` · Intel: search for "Intel Driver & Support Assistant".
Install the driver and restart the computer.

browserUpdate.title: Update your browser
browserUpdate.steps:
Chrome: open `chrome://settings/help`. Edge: open `edge://settings/help`. Firefox: menu ☰ → Help → About Firefox.
The page looks for updates by itself.
Restart the browser when it asks.

gpuChoice.title: Let the browser use the strong graphics card
gpuChoice.steps:
Open the Windows settings: System → Display → Graphics.
Pick your browser in the list, or add it with "Browse".
Click "Options", choose "High performance" and save.
Restart the browser.
gpuChoice.outro: If Windows offers only one graphics chip, your computer has no second one.

power.title: Give the game full power
power.steps:
Plug in the charger.
Windows: Settings → System → Power & battery → Power mode "Best performance".
Chrome: open `chrome://settings/performance` and switch off "Energy Saver". Edge: open `edge://settings/system` and switch off efficiency mode.
Mac: System Settings → Battery, switch off Low Power Mode.

network.title: Make the connection steadier
network.steps:
Use a network cable instead of Wi-Fi, or sit closer to the router.
Pause downloads, cloud sync and video streams on all devices at home.
Switch off a VPN while you play.
Restart the router if the connection drops often.
network.outro: If all players are slow, the server is the bottleneck: tell your GM.

PC.settingsIntro: These settings apply to this computer only. Changes made here can be undone.

settingHint.performanceMode: Low switches off soft light edges and some animations. High and maximum look best and cost the most.
settingHint.maxFPS: Fewer frames per second spare the computer and the battery. 30 is still smooth for a tabletop game.
settingHint.pixelRatioResolutionScaling: On scaled screens Foundry draws with the full screen resolution. Off draws fewer pixels: a bit softer, much lighter. Needs a reload.
settingHint.mipmap: Smoother images when zoomed out, costs graphics memory.

PC.experimentsIntro: Switches one kind of effect off for a few seconds and counts the frames. Shows what costs the most on this computer. The map flickers briefly, nothing is saved.
PC.speedIntro: Downloads a small Foundry image three times (about 5 MB) and measures the speed.
PC.speedResult: Your download speed: {speed}. A map of 50 MB needs about {time}.
PC.speedFailed: The connection test did not work.

light.name: Light
light.hint: Low quality, 30 frames, no animations, no resolution scaling.

minimal.name: Minimal
minimal.hint: Like Light, and without mipmaps. For very weak computers.

verdict.animations: Animations cost the most: {gain} % more frames without them. Turn off light animation.
verdict.videos: Videos cost the most: {gain} % more frames without them. Ask the GM for fewer or smaller videos.
verdict.weather: Weather effects cost the most: {gain} % more frames without them. Lower the particle density in the weather module or ask the GM.
verdict.filters: Module effects cost the most: {gain} % more frames without them. Glows, outlines and similar effects of modules are expensive.
verdict.lighting: Lighting costs the most: {gain} % more frames without it. Lower the graphics quality, it softens light edges less.
verdict.none: No single effect stands out. Your graphics chip is busy with the picture as a whole: lower quality and resolution scaling help most.

Scene.checking: Checking the files of the scene…
Scene.downloadHint: All images and videos of the scene: background, foreground, tiles, tokens.
Scene.largestHint: The longest side of the largest image. Many graphics chips stop at 8192 or 16384 pixels.
Scene.gpuHint: What the images take in graphics memory once drawn.
Scene.unknown: Files whose size could not be read: {count}.
Scene.unreachable: The size could not be read (another server without permission).
Scene.restoreHint: Use the original file again in this scene.
Scene.sounds: Ambient sounds: {bytes}, they load when a token comes near.

Modules.title: Module measurement
Modules.intro: Measures for 15 seconds how much time every module, the system and Foundry itself use on this computer. Keep playing as usual meanwhile: move tokens, open sheets.
Modules.total: Measured for {seconds} s. Scripts used {total} % of the time.
Modules.noLongFrames: Your browser does not report long frames, so event handlers of modules are not counted. Chrome and Edge do.
Modules.gmOnly: Only the GM can switch modules off. Use "Tell the GM" on a finding.
Modules.downloadsIntro: What this browser downloaded in this session outside the canvas (scripts, styles, sounds, pictures in windows), without files from the cache. Images of the canvas count in the scene check.

Startup.title: Loading time
Startup.intro: Measures the next start of Foundry: how long each stage takes and how much each module adds. Foundry reloads for it.
Startup.packages: Time of packages during the start
Startup.done: The start was measured. The result is in the tab Modules.

Players.intro: Every player's computer reports how the game runs there. Ask a player to check with the stethoscope button.
Players.watchHint: Ask all players for fresh numbers every 5 seconds for the next 2 minutes.
Players.askAllHint: Opens the Performance Doctor on every player's computer.
Players.hidden: The tab is in the background
Players.askHint: Open the Performance Doctor on this player's computer
Players.noReport: No report yet (module off, sharing off or older version)
Players.watching: The players send fresh numbers for 2 minutes.
Players.askedAll: All players were asked to check their game.
Players.asked: {name} was asked to check the game.

World.title: World check
World.intro: Measures what every player downloads when joining and finds the largest documents. Takes a moment in large worlds.
World.totalHint: The world data this client received when it joined.
World.diskHint: What the server keeps on its disk, with history.
World.fog: Fog of war on the server: {bytes}

Alert.player: {name} has a problem: {issue}. The tab Players of the Performance Doctor shows more.
Alert.loadFailed: {name} could not load all images of {scene}: {files}

Warn.scene: {scene} is heavy: {bytes} to download, about {typical} on an average line. The Performance Doctor (tab Scene) can make the images smaller.
Warn.sceneSlowest: {scene} is heavy: {bytes} to download. {name} needs about {time}. The Performance Doctor (tab Scene) can make the images smaller.
Warn.image: {file} is large ({bytes}, {px} pixels). Players will wait for it. The Performance Doctor (tab Scene) can make a smaller copy.
Warn.imageGpu: {file} ({px} pixels) is larger than the graphics chip of a player can show ({max} pixels). For that player it may stay black. The Performance Doctor (tab Scene) can make a smaller copy.

Optimize.title: Make the image smaller
Optimize.intro: The doctor makes a WebP copy of {file} and uses it in this scene.
Optimize.others: Also use it in the other scenes with this image ({count})
Optimize.keepsOriginal: The original stays where it is. "Original" in the file list brings it back.
Optimize.notSmaller: The copy is not smaller than the original.
Optimize.question: Use the copy? Scenes that change: {count}.
Optimize.done: Done: {saved} less to download. Scenes using the copy: {count}.
Optimize.failed: The copy could not be made: {reason}

error.toolarge: the image is too large for the browser, choose a smaller size
error.nowebp: this browser cannot save WebP, use Chrome, Edge or Firefox
error.unknownsize: the image size could not be read

Prompt.title: Your game seems slow
Prompt.text: Your game runs at {fps} frames per second. The Performance Doctor finds out why and helps you fix it.
Prompt.off: The doctor will not ask again. You can switch it on in the module settings.

SELFTEST.Title: Performance Doctor self-test
SELFTEST.Hint: Checks the socket, the attribution of hooks, the meter, the browser reports and the texts.
SELFTEST.Attribution: Only {share} % of the hook callbacks have a known owner. Is the module loaded as a library and the attribution switched on?
SELFTEST.NoSystemHooks: No hook callback of {system} has been seen. The system may have loaded before the module.
SELFTEST.Meter: The meter is not on the canvas.
SELFTEST.Resources: The browser does not report downloads.
SELFTEST.NoLongFrames: This browser does not report long frames (Chrome and Edge do).
SELFTEST.Gpu: The graphics chip could not be read.
SELFTEST.Upload: You may not upload files, so smaller copies of images cannot be saved.
SELFTEST.Problems: Self-test: {problems} of {checks} checks found a problem.
SELFTEST.NewVersions: Performance Doctor: Foundry {versions} is newer than the version the module was tested with. Run the self-test in the module settings.
